 (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.3955/2024  JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against the respondents for seeking compensation on account of death of one Sri.Krishna Hanuman @ Krishnappa S/o Hanumantha Rayappa, in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
That on 23.03.2024 at about 04.20 p.m, the said Krishna Hanuman @ Krishnappa was proceeding by walk from Nagarakatte to SSK Circle, on the left side of the road in careful manner by following all the traffic rules, when he reached near Nagarakatte,
Pavagada Town, at that time a Car bearing No.KA-35-N-9214 came to main road of Madhugiri Village Gate - Sira Main Road, which belongs to respondent No.1, driven by its driver in a very high speed, in rash and negligent manner, at very high speed and dashed against said Krishna Hanuman @ Krishnappa.

Due to which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries and immediately after the accident he was shifted to Government hospital, Pavagada and after first aid, he was shifted to Boss hospital,
Bengaluru and taken treatment and then he was again admitted at Government hospital, (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.3955/2024 Pavagada, as inpatient and on 02.05.2024 at about 12.00 p.m the doctor declared that he was dead.
The petitioners have spent Rs.4,00,000/- towards medical and funeral expenses.
Prior to the accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 57 years and was working as Hotel Supplier at Naidu Hotel, Pavagada, as own work and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.

Due to unnatural death of the deceased, the petitioners are Radhamma vs Veeresha M S on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43049815/
2 undergoing irreparable loss and mental agony.
The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending Car and in this regard the Pavagada Police have registered a case against driver of the offending car.
The respondent No.1 is the RC Owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said offending vehicle,
are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- to the petitioners together with interest at the rate of 18% p.a with costs.
03. Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent and hence, was placed exparte.
On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and has filed objections.

04. The respondent No.2 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioners and further (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.3955/2024 denied age, income, occupation of deceased and manner of accident, injuries sustained by the deceased, treatment taken by the deceased, expenses incurred by the petitioners, dependency of the petitioners with the deceased and admits that this respondent has issued policy of insurance in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of Car bearing No.KA-35-N- 9214 and the liability of this respondent if any, is limited to terms and conditions of the policy and contended that the driver of the offending car was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident as on the date of accident and thereby, the owner of the vehicle committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
The car was not at all involved in the accident and the driver of the alleged vehicle was no way related in the alleged accident as on the date of accident.

The compensation claimed is exorbitant and hence, pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.2.
05.

Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following Issues have been framed: -
ISSUES 01.
Whether petitioner proves that she is the LRs/dependents of deceased Sri.Krishna Hanuman @ Krishnappa S/o Hanumantharayappa?

02. Whether petitioners prove that  deceased Sri.Krishna Hanuman @
Krishnappa S/o Hanumantharayappa was died on 23.03.2024 at about 4.20 p.m,
near Nagarkatte, Pawagada Taluk, Tumakuru District, due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing registration No. KA-35-N-9214 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
03. Whether respondent No.2 proves that driver of car not having valid license?
04. Whether respondent No.2 proves that due to the negligence of the deceased accident took place. Hence, respondent No.2 is not liable to pay compensation?

05. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
06 . What order or award?
06. In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.2 got examined himself as PW.1 and got examined MRT as PW.2 and got marked 21 documents as Ex.P.1 to 21 and closed their side evidence.

07. By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.2 counsel submits no oral evidence, hence respondent No.2 evidence is taken as nil and closed its side evidence.
08.
Heard both sides.

My findings on the aforesaid Issues are as under:-

As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS 10. Issue No.1:- Petitioner No.2 filed affidavit stated that, he is the son, petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.3 is the daughter of the deceased.

To prove the said facts, he has produced notarized copies of Aadhaar cards of deceased and other petitioners as per Ex.P.13 to 15 and 18 which shows that the petitioners are the wife, major son and major daughter of the deceased.
As per the recent Judgment of our Hon'ble High Court even the major sons and married daughters are entitled to claim compensation for the death of their parents on all heads.
There is no dispute in her cross-examination regarding relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
So, on perusal of these documents, it is true that the petitioners No.1 to 3 are (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.3955/2024 the legal representatives and dependents on the deceased.
Accordingly, this Issue is answered in the affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:- The petitioner No.2 got himself examined as PW.1 and he has given evidence in the form of the affidavit and he has reiterated the petition averments therein.

Though, he has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioners that due to rash and negligent driving of the offending car by its driver, the deceased has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident and later died.
On perusal of the documents, Ex.P.1 is the FIR registered at Pavagada Police against driver of the offending car.

Ex.P.2 is the Complaint which shows that due to rash and negligent driving by the Radhamma vs Veeresha M S on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43049815/
4 driver of the offending car, the accident took place and deceased sustained injuries.

Ex.P.3 to 5 are Spot Mahazar, Sketch and Seizer Mahazar showing the place of accident Sira - Pavagada Road, near Nagarakatte in front of Hotel Rafika's public road and after investigation the Police have seized the offending car, which is not disputed.
Ex.P.6 is copy of Notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act issued to the owner/driver of the offending Car by name A.V.Purushothama.

Ex.P.7 is (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.3955/2024 copy of Reply to notice which discloses that the owner/driver of the offending Car by name one A.V.Purushothama has stated that he was driving the said car as on the date of accident and he had valid driving licence and said car had valid insurance as on the date of accident.
Ex.P.8 is IMV report shows involvement of offending car in the accident.
Ex.P.9 is Wound certificate shows that deceased sustained six injuries, out of which injury Nos.1, 4, 5 and 6 are grievous and others are simple in nature.

Ex.P.10 is Discharge summary shows deceased sustained 1) Severe traumatic head injury - bilateral sub dural hematoma with right sided mass effect, multiple bifrontal hemorrhagic contusions 2) Left shaft of tibia segmental fracture (Proximal tibia shatzker type - 06 + distal 1/3rd tibia shaft fracture) and 3) Right proximal tibia fracture - shatzker type - 06.
Ex.P.11 is Post mortem report of deceased Krishna Hanuman shows the cause of death is due to internal hemorrhage and sepis due to RTA/prolonged hospital stay.

Ex.P.12 is Charge sheet shows after completion of investigation the Investigation Officer has filed Charge sheet against driver of the offending Car for the offences punishable U/s 279, 304(A) of IPC and Sec.134(a & b) and 187 of IMV Act.
Ex.P.17 is MRI scan.

(SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.3955/2024 The petitioner got examined Medical Records Technician at Boss hospital, Bengaluru, as PW.2 and he has produced Authorization letter, Inpatient case sheet and X-rays as per Ex.P.19 to 21, wherein it is mentioned that "Alleged H/O RTA, hit by 4 wheeler (KA-35-N-9214) while patient was pedestrian around 04.30 p.m on 23.03.2024 near Nagarakatte,
Pavagada, Tumkur District".

The oral and documentary evidence adduced by the petitioners clearly goes to show that the accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of offending car and deceased sustained injuries and later died during the course of treatment.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered in the affirmative.

12. Issues No.3 and 4:- In order to avoid repetition of facts and appreciation of evidence on record,
these Issues are taken together for common consideration and discussion.
13. The respondent No.2 has taken specific contention that the driver of the offending car was not having valid licence and accident occurred due to negligence of deceased.

On perusal of Charge sheet, it is found that the Investigation Officer has not quoted any sections regarding non-possessing of driving (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.3955/2024 licence by the driver of the offending car and the accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased also.
In this regard, the respondent No.2 did not examined any of the witnesses to prove its contention.
Hence, the contention of respondent No.2 is untenable.
Accordingly, Issues No.3 and 4 are answered in the negative.

5 14.
Issue No.5:- This Issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased Krishna Hanuman @ Krishnappa, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

The PW.1/petitioner No.2 has stated that prior to accident deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 57 years and was working as Hotel Supplier at Naidu Hotel, Pavagada, as own work and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m and they have spent Rs.4,00,000/- towards medical and funeral expenses.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners are put to great financial loss, loss of love and affection and mental agony.
15. It is the duty of the petitioners to prove age of the deceased as on the date of accident.
The petitioners have not produced any birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card of the deceased to show the exact date of birth of the deceased.
However, (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.3955/2024 they have produced Ex.P.15 Aadhaar card of deceased.

Even though the said document is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of other evidence, said document can be relied upon and according to which the date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 01.01.1967.
The alleged accident occurred on 23.03.2024 and hence it appears that as on the date of accident the age of the deceased is 57 years.

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 57 years and as per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 56 to 60 years is "9".

sentences.text: 16. So far as avocation and income of deceased is concerned, the petitioners have not placed any materials before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2024 to be taken as Rs.16,500/- p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.3955/2024 income of the deceased is at Rs.16,500/-
and it is multiplied by 12.
17.

In the case on hand, undoubtedly the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the son and petitioner No.3 is the daughter of the deceased and they are the dependents on the earnings of the deceased.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017)
16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case, the future prospects or additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since deceased was aged 57 years at the time of accident and he comes in the age group of 50 to 60 years and was self employee, 10% income should be added to the monthly income towards future prospects which would be result in the income to be (16,500 + 1,650) = Rs.18,150/-.

Therefore, considering the materials available on record, this tribunal is of the opinion that since there are three dependents, it is appropriate to deduct 1/3rd of the income towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (Rs.18,150 - Rs.6,050) = Rs.12,100/-.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.12,100/-.
As the deceased was aged about (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.3955/2024 57 years, the multiplier of 9 would have to be applied.

Consequently the claimants would be entitled for a sum of (Rs.12,100 x 12 x 9)
Rs.13,06,800/- is awarded towards loss of dependency.

6 18.
Medical expenses:- The petitioners have produced entire Medical bills as per Ex.P.16 for Rs.2,33,650/-.
To disprove the medical bills, the respondent No.2 has not produced any documents nor any evidence.
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for Rs.2,33,650/- under this head.

19. In view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & Others case, in respect to loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every 3 years.

Accordingly, in the head of loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses,
10% is enhanced for period of every 3 years.
20. The claimant No.1 is the wife and claimants No.2 and 3 are the children of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.48,400/- towards loss of spousal consortium.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.3955/2024 Nanu Ram alias Churu Ram reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, the petitioners No.2 and 3 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of parental consortium and petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses and transportation of dead body.

sentences.text:
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and noticing the number of dependents and 1/3rd of the income taken into consideration towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased, this Tribunal has placed reliance on ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & others case has calculated compensation as under;
 Sl. Head of Compensation Amount in  No. Rs.
 1. Loss of Dependency 13,06,800-00  (After deducting 1/3rd of the  income towards personal  and living expenses)
 2
Medical expenses 2,33,650-00  3. Loss of spousal consortium 48,400-00  (For petitioner No.1)
4 . Loss of parental consortium 80,000-00  (For petitioners No.2 and 3)
5. Loss of estate 18,150-00
6 . Towards transportation of 18,150-00  deadbody and funeral  expenses  Total 17,05,150-00 21.
Accordingly I hold that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.17,05,150/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
22. Regarding liability:- Despite sufficient opportunity, the respondent No.1 remained absent and was placed exparte.
On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared and filed objections and Radhamma vs Veeresha M S on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43049815/
7 contested the matter, but not lead evidence to disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove its contention.
On the date of accident policy was in force.
Hence, respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay above said compensation amount.
Respondent No.2 Insurance Company is directed to deposit above said compensation amount within two months from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.5 partly in affirmative.

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 to 5, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.17,05,150/- (Rupees Seventeen lakhs five thousand one hundred and fifty only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

The petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioners No.2 and 3 are the major son and daughter of the deceased were apportioned the compensation in the ratio of 70-15-15, in the award amount together with interest.

On deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 is entitled to get release 70% of the award through E-payment directly to her account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in her (SCCH-3) 18 M.V.C.No.3955/2024 name.
The petitioner No.1 is at liberty to draw periodical interest.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the award amount of petitioners No.2 and 3 are meager one, entire award amount is ordered to be released in their favour through E-payment directly to their account by obtaining their bank account details.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

10% is enhanced for period of every 3 years.

5. Loss of estate 18,150-00

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.17,05,150/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
22. Regarding liability:- Despite sufficient opportunity, the respondent No.1 remained absent and was placed exparte.
On the date of accident policy was in force.
Hence, respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay above said compensation amount.
Respondent No.2 Insurance Company is directed to deposit above said compensation amount within two months from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.5 partly in affirmative.
In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 to 5, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.17,05,150/- (Rupees Seventeen lakhs five thousand one hundred and fifty only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.
The petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioners No.2 and 3 are the major son and daughter of the deceased were apportioned the compensation in the ratio of 70-15-15, in the award amount together with interest.
On deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 is entitled to get release 70% of the award through E-payment directly to her account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in her (SCCH-3) 18 M.V.C.No.3955/2024 name.
The petitioner No.1 is at liberty to draw periodical interest.
On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the award amount of petitioners No.2 and 3 are meager one, entire award amount is ordered to be released in their favour through E-payment directly to their account by obtaining their bank account details.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
